annotations.title: Re-file a bank line (preview, then confirm)

description: Re-file a bank line that was already filed wrongly: reverses everything it posted (one reversal journal on the line's date, payments taken back off invoices/bills) and files it again to the new target. Same target arguments as accounting_file_bank_line. TWO STEPS: first call = preview of the reversal and new journal + confirm_token; second call with confirm_token does it. Changes the user's real books — only after they have seen the preview and agreed. Needs the user's GetAccountED sign-in (they are asked to sign in the first time).

account_code.description: New target: file straight to this account (chart of accounts code)

allocations.description: New target: which invoices (money in) or bills (money out) this pays, with optional amounts (part payments allowed). Omit amount to settle as much as is due, in order.

amount.description: Rand allocated to this invoice or bill

business_id.description: Accounting practices only: which client's books (an id from accounting_list_my_businesses). Leave out to use the books chosen at sign-in.

confirm_token.description: Second step only: the token from the preview

customer_id.description: New target: customer id — for a receipt; anything not allocated goes on account

on_account.description: Whole amount on account with the customer / supplier

refund.description: With account_code: money in that is a refund of an expense

supplier_id.description: New target: supplier contact id — for a supplier payment

supplier_name.description: New target: supplier known only by name on its bills

vat.description: With account_code: split 15% VAT out of the amount (VAT vendors only). Omit to use the default for that account.

name: accounting_refile_bank_line
